2  Crl.Misc.113/2018  JUDGMENT
The present petition is filed by the petitioners under Sec.12 of Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005.

entities.text: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
2. The brief facts of the petitioner's case are as under; The petitioner is the legally wedded wife of respondent and their marriage was solemnized on 08.10.2015 at Classic Mall Function hall, Jamniya Rabiya Bee vs Afsar on 30 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120808750/
1
Tipu Masjid, Hegade Nagar, Bangalore.
Further she submitted that, from the wed lock petitioner gave birth to female child by name Meher Taj.
Further she submitted that, at the time of marriage respondent has received a sum of Rs.1 lakh as a dowry and golden ornaments worth about Rs.4 lakhs and household items worth about Rs.1 lakhs.
Entire marriage expenses of sum of Rs.3 lakhs borne by her parents.
Further she submitted that, on the instigation of the respondent's family members restarted to demanding further dowry and sites etc., and respondent started ill treating the petitioner.

For that she has filed a private complaint in PCR No.3280/18 before IV ACMM,
Bangalore for an offences punishable U/Sec.498A, 307, 120B, 504, 506 of IPC.

Further she submitted that, respondent is driving a own auto Crl.Misc.113/2018 rickshaw and earning Rs.1,000/- per day and also doing other works and he is getting a monthly income of Rs.30,000/- to Rs.40,000/- per month.
In spite of having sufficient source of income, he has failed to maintain the petitioner and minor daughter.
Further she submitted that, at present petitioner and her daughter are residing at her parents house, they are also expressing the difficulties to maintain the petitioner and her child.
Further she submitted that, petitioner being a house wife she is finding difficult to maintain herself and minor child.
Hence, on all these grounds she filed this petition.

3. After the service of notice, respondent appeared before this court through his counsel and respondent filed statement of objection and in the statement of objection he has admitted his relationship with the petitioner.
Further, he denied all other allegations against him and his family members.
Further he submitted that, he and his family members never demanded dowry from the petitioner and they never caused domestic violence against the petitioner.
Hence, he prays to reject the petition filed by the petitioner.
The petitioner to substantiate her case has examined herself as PW.1 and got marked Ex.P.1 to 8.
The respondent has not led his evidence in spite of sufficient opportunities.
5. Heard arguments on petitioner's sides.

Point No.1: In a domestic violence case the petitioner has to prove the domestic relationship Crl.Misc.113/2018 between herself and respondent, she was residing with the respondent in a shared household, the domestic violence was caused by the respondent upon her.
The respondent has neglected the petitioner without any reasonable cause and the respondent is capable to provide maintenance to the petitioner.
9. In this case, there is no dispute regarding the relationship between parties.
Hence, it is proved that the petitioner and the respondent are in domestic relationship.

It is also an admitted fact that,
the petitioner and respondent resided together till the date of separation.
Hence they have resided together in a shared household.
Only the aspect of domestic violence by respondent needs to be proved by the petitioner.

10. In order to prove that, the respondent has committed domestic violence, the petitioner has examined herself as P.W.1 and filed her affidavit in lieu of examination in chief wherein she has reiterated the contents of her petition.
She has produced 8 documents and got them marked as Ex.P.1 to 8.

Ex.P.1 & 1(a) is the certified copy of the Nikhanama along with translation copy, Ex.P.2 is the certified copy of the marriage invitation card, Ex.P.3 is the certified copy of the Aadhar Crl.Misc.113/2018 card of the petitioner, Ex.P.4 is the certified copy of the birth certificate of the daughter of the petitioner, Ex.P.5 are the certified copies of the photographs of the wedding, Ex.P.6 is the certified copy of the FIR in Crime No.67/2021 registered by Sampigehalli police for the offence punishable U/Sec.498-A, 307, 120(b), 420, 504, 506 R/w 34 of IPC, Ex.P.7 is the certified copy of PCR No.1467/2020 on the file of the Hon'ble 7th ACMM, Ex.P.8 is the certified copy of the complaint filed in PCR No.1467/2020 before Hon'ble 7th ACMM.
The respondent has filed his statement of objections and denied all the allegations made by the petitioner.
11. The respondent has not cross examined P.W.1 in spite of sufficient opportunities.
Hence, Cross Examination of PW.1 is taken as nil.
Thereafter, respondent has not led his evidence in spite of sufficient opportunities.
Hence, respondent's evidence is taken as nil.
The respondent has not advanced their arguments as well.

12. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Vidyadhar V/s Manik Rao reported in 1999 (3) SCC 573 has held that "where a party to the suit does not appear into the witness box and state his own case on oath and does not Crl.Misc.113/2018 offer himself to be cross examined by the other side, a presumption would arise that the case set up by him is not correct as has been held in a series of decisions passed by various High Courts and the Privy Council....."

entities.text: Vidyadhar V/s Manik Rao reported in 1999 (3) SCC 573
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, if a party abstains from entering the witness box it would give raise to an adverse inference against such party U/Sec.114 of Indian Evidence Act.

By applying this proposition of law to the present case it is seen that the respondent did not appear before the Court and state his case on oath and offer himself to be cross examined in spite of sufficient opportunities.
Hence, an adverse inference has to be drawn against respondent U/Sec.114 of Indian Evidence Act and the Court is compelled to conclude that the case set up by the respondent is false.
Further respondent has not cross examined PW.1/petitioner.

3 13.

entities.text: Rabiya Bee vs Afsar on 30 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Petitioner has mainly alleged that, the respondent has demanded dowry and harassed her.

Hence, she was constrained to file private compliant against him in PCR No.1467/2020 on the file of Hon'ble 7th ACMM, Bangalore and on the direction of the Hon'ble 7th ACMM, FIR has been registered by Sampigehalli police station against the respondent for the offences punishable U/Sec.498-A, 307, 120(b), 420, 504, 506 Crl.Misc.113/2018 R/w 34 of IPC.
Petitioner has produced Ex.P.6 to 8 in this regard.
Since, the respondent has not cross examined the petitioner said documents are unchallenged.
In the said complaint marked as Ex.P.8 petitioner has specifically alleged that respondent has harassed her for dowry and he has thrown her out of the house.
She has alleged that, the respondent has threatened to marry some other girl by stating that the petitioner is not good looking.
Respondent has not cross examined the petitioner hence all the allegations made by the petitioner in the petition have to be accepted by this Court.
If the respondents wanted to deny the said allegations he would have appeared before this court and would have challenged the same but he has not done so.
Further, the respondents have not denied any of the allegations in the petition and hence these allegations have remained uncontroverted and they are proved.

14. Since the proceedings under domestic violence Act are quasi criminal and quasi civil in nature the evidence on record has to be decided on the basis of preponderance of probabilities and court should not look for proof beyond reasonable doubt.
In this case the conduct of the respondent in not appearing before the Crl.Misc.113/2018 Court and contesting the matter probabalizes the allegations made by the petitioner.
15. In the present case respondent who is the husband of petitioner and father of her child has not paid any maintenance to the petitioner and her child from the date of separation.
As already stated this constitutes economic abuse as contemplated in PWDV Act.
Therefore, it is proved that the respondent has committed domestic violence against the petitioner.
Hence, point No.1 answered in the affirmative.
16. POINT No.2 :- The petitioner in this case has sought for Rs.20,000/- monthly maintenance for herself and the child U/Sec.20 of PWDV Act.
Admittedly, the petitioner is not employed.
The petitioner in her assets and liability affidavit has stated that, she is incurring expenses of Rs.15,000/- per month towards food, clothing, medical, shelter.
She has submitted that, she is residing in her parents house.
In spite of sufficient opportunities respondent has not filed assets and liabilities affidavit.

It is the contention of the petitioner that, the respondent is earning Rs.1,000/-
per day from his own auto rickshaw and he also has income from his own houses and he is also doing other business works.
Crl.Misc.113/2018
She has stated that respondent has his own property at Bangalore.
As already stated that the respondent has not cross examined the petitioner.
Hence, he has not been able to prove any of his contentions.
Since, respondent has not filed his assets and liabilities affidavit an adverse inference has to be drawn against the respondent.
17. As per Sec.106 of Indian Evidence Act only the respondent will have special knowledge about his income and he has to prove that, he does not have sufficient income to maintain the petitioner.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As discussed in point No.1 the petitioner was compelled to leave her matrimonial home and under the said circumstance she was forced to set up a new life for herself and the child.
The petitioner has stated that, she requires an accommodation and she has sought for Rs.4,000/- as rent per month.
Being the husband of the petitioner the respondent is duty bound to secure an accommodation or pay rent to the petitioner.
As per the Assets and liabilities affidavit the petitioner is residing at her parents house.
The parents of the petitioner are not duty bound to maintain the petitioner.
Hence, even though the petitioner is residing at her parents house the Crl.Misc.113/2018 respondent is still bound to arrange for an accommodation in favour of the petitioner.
19. It is proved by discussion in point No.1 that, the respondent has committed domestic violence against the petitioner.
The respondent has not paid any maintenance to the petitioner till now.
There is no straight jacket formula to award maintenance.

As per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Rajanesh V/s Neha reported in (2021) 2 SCC 324, the Court has to consider the status of the parties, earning capacity of the parties, needs and expenses of the petitioner, number of dependents on the respondent, expenses of the respondent, educational qualification of the parties,
whether the petitioner has independent source and whether the same is sufficient to enable her to maintain herself, standard of living as she was accustomed to in the matrimonial home, whether she was working before marriage, cost of litigation, while ordering for maintenance.

entities.text: Rajanesh V/s Neha reported in (2021) 2 SCC 324
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: For the sake of argument if the Court presumes that the respondent has no income even then he is duty bound to maintain his wife and child as held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Anju Garg V/s Deepak Kumar Garg reported in 2022 Livelaw (SC) 805 , wherein it is held that, the husband is required to earn money Crl.Misc.113/2018 even by physical labor if he is able bodied and could not avoid his obligation except on legally permissible grounds mentioned in the statues.

entities.text: Anju Garg V/s Deepak Kumar Garg reported in 2022 Livelaw (SC) 805
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, he cannot avoid maintaining the petitioner and her child.

20. Further, U/Sec.20 of PWDV Act the Magistrate has power to direct the respondent to pay monetary relief to meet the expenses incurred by the petitioner and losses suffered by her and any child of the petitioner as a result of domestic violence and such relief may interalia include the maintenance for the aggrieved person as well as children if any including an order under or in addition to an order of maintenance U/Sec.125 of Cr.PC or any other law for the time being in force.
U/Sec.20(2) the monetary relief has to be adequate, fair and reasonable and consistent with the standard of living in which the aggrieved person is accustomed.
Further, it is the moral, legal responsibility of the husband to maintain his wife.

Applying these propositions of law, the respondent is directed to pay Rs.5,000/- per month each to the petitioner and her minor child by name Meher Taj towards maintenance and respondent is also directed to pay Rs.4,000/- per month to the petitioner towards the rent.
The petitioner has sought for direction to the respondent to pay compensation and damages of Rs.10,00,000/- for the physical and mental torture suffered at the hands of the respondent.

Sec.22 of PWDV Act states, Magistrate may grant compensation in addition to the other reliefs that may be granted under this Act and direct the respondents to pay compensation and damages for injuries including mental torture and emotional distress caused by the acts of domestic violence committed Rabiya Bee vs Afsar on 30 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120808750/
5 by the respondent.

As discussed in point No.1 it is proved that the respondent has subjected the petitioner to domestic violence and she has incurred litigation expenses as well due to the acts of respondent and she has undergone severe hardship and mental agony.
Hence, respondent is directed to pay an amount of Rs.2,00,000/- (Rupees two lakhs only) to the petitioner towards compensation.
Hence, point No.2 answered partly in the affirmative.

22. POINT No.3 :- In view of the materials placed before this court, pleadings, deposition and documentary evidence this court proceed to pass the following;
Crl.Misc.113/2018 ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner under Sec.12 of The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 is allowed in part.

sentences.text:
Respondent is hereby directed to pay an amount of Rs.5,000/- per month (Rupees five thousand only) towards maintenance and Rs.4,000/-(Rupees four thousand only) towards rent to the petitioner from the date of filing of the petition till her lifetime or her remarriage whichever is earlier.
Further, respondent is hereby directed to pay an amount of Rs.5,000/-per month (Rupees five thousand only) to the petitioner's child by name Meher Taj towards maintenance from the date of filing of the petition till her marriage.
Further, respondent is directed to pay an amount of Rs.2,00,000/- (Rupees two lakhs only) to the petitioner towards Crl.Misc.113/2018 compensation within 3 months from the date of this order.
Office is directed to furnish a copy of this order free of cost to the petitioner.
(Dictated to the stenographer directly on computer, typed by her, corrected and then pronounced by me in open court on this the 30th day of May 2024).
(AKHILA H.K.) MMTC-VI BENGALURU.
